data.title: Grab to expand Singapore AV fleet fivefold to 50 vehicles
data.description:
It also plans to launch an on-demand, point-to-point AV service in selected Punggol locations.

Grab will expand its autonomous vehicle (AV) fleet in Singapore fivefold to 50 vehicles over the next six months, from its current fleet of 10.

The company will also expand its AV service coverage within Punggol in collaboration with the Ministry of Transport (MOT) and Land Transport Authority (LTA), with plans to extend the service to other parts of Singapore subject to regulatory approvals.

The expansion follows the performance of Grab’s initial fleet of 10 WeRide GXR vehicles, which have logged more than 110,000 kilometres of autonomous mileage on Singapore roads and served over 12,000 unique riders. Grab said 99% of riders surveyed would recommend the service.

LTA approved Grab and WeRide to launch Community Rides, an AV shuttle service in Punggol, in January 2026, followed by Public Rides in April.

Grab said more than 1,000 people are on its waitlist for new AV experiences, with riders seeking more locations, direct routes and flexible booking options.

The company, with LTA’s support, is preparing to launch an on-demand, point-to-point AV service across selected Punggol locations, with additional service points expected to be added in the coming months.

“We continue to evolve and build our service by responding to direct feedback from the community, and by drawing on data and technology from our popular ride-hailing business,” said Alex Hungate, president and chief operating officer at Grab. “As a homegrown company deeply rooted in this region, we will introduce AVs in a way that complements our driver network, whilst also unlocking new career pathways for our local workforce.”

Grab is also investing in AV infrastructure, including working with government agencies to establish an AV depot in Punggol.

Its training arm, GrabAcademy, and WeRide have developed training pathways for driver and delivery partners interested in moving into AV-related roles.

To date, 30 Safety Operators have been certified, including six who have also qualified as Remote Operators. Some have progressed into supervisory and trainer positions.

Grab said hundreds of new AV roles will be created as it explores establishing Singapore as a regional centre of excellence for AV localisation and deployment. The company is also developing talent in areas including design, engineering and operations.

The fleet expansion forms part of Grab’s hybrid mobility strategy, which aims to have AVs and human-driven vehicles complement each other to increase network capacity.

Grab said it will continue strengthening its human-driver network through initiatives including fleet electrification partnerships under GrabRentals and GrabCab, as well as vehicle financing through its Car Marketplace.

The company said the expansion is a step towards its goal of deploying thousands of AVs across Southeast Asia by 2030.

data.title: Data concerns delay AI scaling for over half of organisations: OneTrust
data.description:
Firms are also dealing with challenges around visibility and risk management.

More than half of Singapore organisations cite data-related concerns as delaying artificial intelligence (AI) deployment despite the country leading in AI governance maturity, according to a OneTrust report. 

About 57% say data quality, access, privacy, or security concerns have most delayed their ability to launch or scale AI initiatives.

Organisations are also dealing with challenges around visibility, risk management, and maintaining consistent controls.

Governance should be built into AI systems and processes from the outset rather than introduced after an incident or once a tool has already been adopted, said Arran Mulvaney, OneTrust’s Regional Director for Southeast Asia and India.

“Singapore has moved beyond the question of whether businesses should adopt AI,” Mulvaney said. 

“The real test now is whether governance can keep pace with the speed they are deploying it,” he added.

Overall, 41% of Singapore organisations surveyed have integrated governance into the AI lifecycle, the highest share amongst the eight markets covered.

About 33% said their firms are using AI across multiple business functions. However, almost half (46%) believe employees have used unapproved applications because approved tools or processes were not available quickly enough.

The report surveyed 1,200 senior business decision-makers across Singapore, Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Spain, the UK, and the US.

data.title: Bond issuance rises 21.8% to record $120.8b in 2025
data.description:
MAS cites refinancing needs and capital demand for AI, technology, and infrastructure.

Singapore’s bond market issuance rose $21.8% year-on-year to a record $120.8b (US$95b) in 2025, surpassing the previous high of $97.9b (US$77b) set in 2023. 

The growth was attributed to refinancing needs and regional demand for capital to fund artificial intelligence, technology, and infrastructure investments, according to the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS).

The $120.8b (US$95b) figure covers long-term Singapore dollar and non-Singapore dollar bond issuances, MAS said in a corporate debt market development update.

Separately, total new debt issuance arranged by financial institutions in Singapore, including short-term debt, increased 10% to $339b from $308b in 2024.

Outstanding debt arranged by financial institutions grew 6.8% to $659b at the end of 2025, from $617b a year earlier.

The US dollar remained the main issuance currency, accounting for 65.56% of the total, followed by the Singapore dollar at 21.4%. 

The euro made up 3.92%, sterling 2.79%, Australian dollar 2.35%, and Hong Kong dollar 1.35%.

Financial institutions remain the largest issuers across both Singapore dollar and non-Singapore dollar markets.

They accounted for 64.9% of Singapore dollar issuance in 2025, whilst property companies made up 10.3%, followed by statutory boards at 9.6%, corporate special purpose vehicles at 9.4%, and non-property companies at 5.8%.

In the non-Singapore dollar market, financial institutions accounted for 77.9% of issuance, followed by non-property companies at 14.5%.

Singapore dollar issuance by financial institutions increased by $10.8b from a year earlier, whilst corporate issuance rose by $6.6b.

MAS said the Singapore dollar market attracted first-time issuers from digital infrastructure, private capital and consumer finance. These included Equinix Asia Financing Corp., Wee Hur Holdings, and IREIT Global.

$1 = US$0.79

data.title: Singapore to add 23,100 migrant worker dormitory beds by 2027
data.description:
Current capacity stood at around 467,000 beds across 1,600 dormitories as of June 2026.

Singapore will release two new Purpose-Built Dormitory (PBD) sites that are expected to provide an estimated 23,100 beds, as the government works to expand accommodation capacity for migrant workers.

The Lorong Lada Hitam 1 site, spanning 10.7 hectares (ha), will provide an estimated 15,000 beds under a 30-year lease.

It is expected to be launched by the first quarter of 2027.

The second site, Jurong Apartments at 529 Upper Jurong Road, covers two ha and has an estimated capacity of 8,100 beds.

It will also have a 30-year lease and is expected to be launched in the second half of 2027.

Together, the two sites will add an estimated 23,100 beds to the pipeline.

As of June 2026, Singapore has approximately 1,600 dormitories providing around 467,000 beds for migrant workers.

The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and Ministry of National Development (MND) announced in March that JTC would launch three PBD sites in 2026 and the first quarter of 2027.

Lok Yang Way and Gali Batu have since been launched as of June 2026.

Across six PBDs launched between the fourth quarter of 2025 and September 2027, around 48,300 beds are expected to be added to the market by the early 2030s.

The government will also introduce four new Quick Build Dormitories (QBDs), with around 16,000 beds in total, expected to become operational in 2027.

MOM’s second PBD at Sengkang West, which will provide 7,200 beds, is expected to be operational by mid-2028.

Combined, the six PBDs, the Sengkang West site, and four QBDs are expected to add around 71,500 beds between 2027 and the early 2030s.

In the near term, the government will temporarily extend leases of existing dormitories and facilitate factory-converted dormitories, construction temporary quarters, and temporary occupation license quarters, subject to infrastructure capacity and land availability.

MOM is also studying a temporary relaxation of occupancy limits under the New Dormitory Standards and will provide an update to the industry in due course.

MOM and MND said they will provide annual updates on the dormitory supply pipeline to support industry planning and participation in upcoming tenders.

data.title: Two Lucky Plaza strata shops put up for sale at $11.4m
data.description:
Units may be bought together or separately from $5.7m each. 

Two adjoining freehold strata shops on the ground floor of Lucky Plaza have been put up for sale at a guide price of $11.4m.

The units may be purchased together or separately, with each shop priced from $5.7m, according to marketing agent CBRE.

The guide price translates to about $13,000 psf based on the combined strata area. 

Each unit has a strata area of about 441 square feet and comes with food and beverage approval.

The shops are located near the atrium of Lucky Plaza, a freehold mixed-use development along Orchard Road with a six-storey retail podium.

The sale will be conducted through an Expression of Interest exercise. It will close on Thursday, 15 October.

No Additional Buyer’s Stamp Duty or Seller’s Stamp Duty will apply to the acquisition.

Foreigners and corporate entities are eligible to buy the properties.

data.title: All-Link H1 2026 net profit sinks 19.8% despite revenue jump
data.description:
Malaysia added $3.53m in revenue after the 2025 acquisition.

All-Link Air & Sea Limited’s (All-Link) net profit attributable to owners of the company fell 19.8% year-on-year (YoY) to $2.95m (US$2.32m) in the first half (H1) of 2026.

Revenue rose 38.2% to $50.93m (US$40.1m), driven by organic volume expansion across existing operations and the initial full-period contribution from its Malaysia operations.

The Malaysia operations contributed $3.53m (US$2.78m) following the August 2025 acquisition of MF Logistics Sdn Bhd’s freight forwarding business.

Gross profit rose 28% YoY to $3.01m (US$4.62m), whilst gross profit margin fell 0.9 percentage points (ppt) to 11.5%.

Profit after tax (PAT) decreased 21.4% to (US$2.37m), whilst adjusted PAT grew 11.6% to $4.29m (US$3.38m).

Adjusted net profit margin slipped 2 ppt to 8.4%. Basic and diluted earnings per share were 2.64 Singapore cents (2.08 US cents), down 19.7% YoY from 3.29 Singapore cents (2.59 US cents).

Core freight forwarding services expanded by 34.4% YoY to $47.63m (US$37.5m), representing 93.6% of H1’s total revenue.

Other third-party logistics services surged by 133.2% YoY to $3.26m (US$2.57m) from $1.40m (US$1.10m), driven by heightened demand for cross-border logistics management and value-added warehousing support within the regional e-commerce supply chain.

Other income grew by 66.4% YoY to $0.90m (US$0.71m) from $0.55m (US$0.43m), primarily lifted by a $0.48m (US$0.38m) non-operating gain recognised on the final settlement of contingent purchase consideration for the Malaysia acquisition.

The group’s cash and bank balances stood at $25.27m (US$19.9m) as at 30 June, whilst its SGX Mainboard listing subsequently raised $20.1m in gross proceeds, strengthening its financial position.

It is also advancing its proposed acquisition of a 30% stake in Vietnam ALLLink-TNR International Logistics Co., Ltd., whilst expanding into Thailand and intending to establish a subsidiary in Indonesia.

“Looking ahead, the Group expects a stronger second half, reflecting the seasonal peak in shipment volumes during the key festive periods in the fourth quarter,” All-Link said.

It expects FY2026 revenue to be higher than FY2025, barring unforeseen circumstances.

(US$1 = SG$1.27)

data.title: SG's PathFin.ai AI-sharing programme grows to over 300 participants
data.description:
The initiative aims to lower the cost for smaller financial institutions adopting AI. 

The Monetary Authority of Singapore’s (MAS) PathFin.ai programme to share artificial intelligence (AI) solutions has grown to over 300 participants since its launch in August 2025. 

“Smaller financial institutions can lower the cost and effort of finding and deploying effective AI solutions,” said MAS Managing Director Chia Der Jiun at the Global FinTech Fest 2026 on 11 September.

The programme was previously reported in October to have brought together more than 80 financial institutions to share their experiences and strategies in using AI. 

Its initial use cases covered areas including sales and marketing, customer operations, risk management, and engineering and technology.

“If a solution has been validated and works, we want to make it easier for others to find and implement it,” Chia added.

MAS is also testing AI models with law enforcement and the banking industry, using cross-bank and public-private data to detect suspicious accounts and transactions in near real time. 

“The aim is to detect sooner, intervene faster, and reduce losses,” Chia said. “We expect to have findings from this work by the end of this year.”

data.title: OCBC tops Forbes' 2026 World's Top Performing Banks list
data.description:
DBS takes second place ahead of HDFC Bank and China Merchants Bank.

Singapore’s OCBC ranked first amongst Tier 1 global banks in Forbes’ inaugural World’s Top Performing Banks 2026 list.

DBS placed second in the same category, putting the two Singapore-headquartered lenders ahead of Mumbai’s HDFC Bank, Shenzhen’s China Merchants Bank, and New York’s JPMorganChase.

Tier 1 covers banks with more than $634.5b (US$500b) in total assets. A total of 24 institutions were included in the category.

The ranking, compiled by Forbes in partnership with market research firm Statista, assessed banks using financial data rather than customer survey results.

Banks were evaluated across profitability, capital and funding resilience, asset quality and efficiency, and growth and earnings quality.

Overall, 500 institutions from 89 countries were included in the 2026 ranking.

$1 = US$0.79

data.title: Reclaims Global net profit climbs 53.1% to $3.8m in H1
data.description:
Revenue jumped 52.9% to $33.3m from $21.8m.

Reclaims Global Limited’s net profit jumped 53.1% year-on-year to $3.8m in the first half ended 31 July 2026, up from $2.5m.

Revenue rose 52.9% to $33.3m from $21.8m a year earlier, whilst profit before tax climbed 64.9% to $4.7m from $2.9m.

Excavation Services remained the largest revenue contributor, increasing 47.3% to $24.1m from $16.4m.

Revenue from Logistics and Leasing grew 52% to $7.2m from $4.8m, whilst Recycling revenue surged 171.9% to $1.7m from $600,000.

Higher business volumes also lifted the group’s costs, including materials, services, and consumables as well as employee expenses.

Reclaims Global said it was more selective in bidding for new projects during the first quarter amidst volatile energy prices. 

Higher diesel costs were factored in for later tenders, it added.

The group completed two freehold property investments during the half, including the $35.1m acquisition of Lasidon Holdings Pte. Ltd., which owns a commercial property at 291 Serangoon Road. 

It also bought an industrial property at 464 Tagore Industrial Avenue for $20.5m.

Reclaims Global declared an interim dividend of 0.25 cents per share.
